question: When present continuous velocity observations are withheld at both training and evaluation, does a learned non-token history GRU use factual temporal information to outperform equally supervised and trained same-capacity current-only GRU on true external CartPole action consequences?
null: P19 GRU perfect return is explainable by contemporaneous public velocity; a newly trained velocity-blind GRU does not exceed matched current-only history-disabled control by >=15 real reward steps and original velocity-blind history-reversed negative by >=10 on each initialization.

inputs.source: Original S29 read-only MIT Gymnasium CartPole-v1 pinned source, same real reset/step, no new simulator
inputs.all_model_visible: 4 public observations with indices 1 (cart velocity) and 3 (angular velocity) replaced by 0 at every timestep; previous completed real action and reward preserved; original full source observations never passed into learned model
inputs.teacher: P18 fixed present-source theta + 0.5*true public angular velocity: human-designed labels recorded from factual expert trajectory; privileged relative to learner-visible zeroed velocity, but same labels delivered to all learned arms; NOT factual-reward-only training
inputs.finite_difference: Hardcoded causal finite difference of two completed, allowed visible theta observations, nominal fixed 0.02-step spacing; may not inspect source physics engine or hidden state
inputs.masks: Current-only GRU trained and evaluated with previous 7 history rows zeroed; full GRU receives last 8 completed rows. Both have exactly 489 parameters and same training optimizer/labels/budgets.
inputs.strict: Mask velocities before all learner forward calls in both supervised training and real environment eval; no reintroduction through unmasked recent row, no model future action access.
